evidence: Nirvana recorded the Velvet Underground's 'Here She Comes Now' (from 'White Light/White Heat', 1968) for the 1991 tribute compilation 'Heaven and Hell: A Tribute to The Velvet Underground', released as a split single with the Melvins' 'Venus in Furs'.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: The Velvet Underground's original is short, quiet and droning, almost a lullaby. Nirvana play it slow and heavy, with thick distorted guitar, and stretch it out. Listen for how the same two chords can go from New York art-rock drone to Seattle sludge. On the other side of the same single, the Melvins played 'Venus in Furs'.

explanation.age13: In 1991 Nirvana recorded a Velvet Underground song, 'Here She Comes Now', for a tribute album. It came out on a single with the Melvins playing another Velvet Underground song on the other side.
explanation.adult: A plain cover edge. It is worth having because it puts the Velvets, the Melvins and Nirvana on one record in 1991, the year 'Nevermind' came out.
